items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: one time we were doing a clinic with the Thad Jones saxophone section... And then Ron Bridgewater said something

ctx.x: I guess, sure. I mean I was never good enough to copy anybody so I just probably — in the words of Pepper Adams, one time we were doing a clinic with the Thad Jones saxophone section. We had about 200 saxophone players in the room. So I said, “We © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

can’t give you a saxophone lesson in an hour and a half, but if you ask some questions, you’ll get five different answers from professionals and that will maybe give you a real idea of what your answer is and whether it’s career minded or whatever it is, music or whatever.” So somebody asked the question, “Who do you copy when you’re learning to improvise?” And I think Billy Harper says, “Well I don’t copy anybody you know.
